ev.q: Among the 6.7% of respondents who reported severe vision impairment, 46.7% reported a fall, ranging from 30.8% in Hawaii to 59.1% in California.
Among all respondents, 28.9% reported at least one fall in the previous year
Respondents were dichotomized into either those in the last year who did or those who did not fall.
found that 28.9% of respondents reported at least one fall in the previous year.
46.7% of adults aged ≥65 years with severe vision impairment fell, compared with 27.7% of those without severe vision impairment.
The differences were statistically significant in all but six U.S. states (Alaska, Delaware, Hawaii, Idaho, Vermont, and Wisconsin).
Weighted estimates, age adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.

equity.level_reason: Age only defines the population (≥65 years) and is used for age adjustment. Severe vision impairment is analyzed as a clinical exposure, not framed as disability as social position or access.

level_alternative.reason: If severe vision impairment is read as disability, group-specific fall prevalences by it are reported and described without disparity framing (capped at 2).

equity.equity_measurement: Comparison is by self-reported severe vision impairment and state; states are geography, not an SPD. Age adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.

notes: The prepass diagnostic-accuracy cue is a false hit ('contrast sensitivity'). The state range is reported with p<0.001, but it is unclear whether that test is across states or with vs without impairment. Vision impairment is treated as a clinical exposure, not disability as social position.
view_issues: The p<0.001 attached to the state ranges does not say which contrast it tests. In the CSV, column headers have inconsistent spacing ('No .§', '% 95% CI').
